title: Amplifying a randomized decision advantage
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine, let $L$ be a language of bit strings, and let $s:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose $\delta,\varepsilon$ are positive rational numbers, $N$ uses at most $s(|x|)$ space on every input and choice word, and for each input $x$ there is a time bound $T$ such that every choice word of length $T$ makes $N$ halt and the probability that it outputs the indicator of membership of $x$ in $L$ is at least $\frac12+\delta$. Then there are a natural number $a$ and a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N'$ using at most $a s(|x|)$ space such that, for every $x$, some time bound $T$ makes every choice word of length $T$ halt and the probability that $N'$ outputs the membership indicator of $x$ in $L$ is at least $1-\varepsilon$.
